questions.q: Which layer of the aortic wall first tears in an acute aortic dissection?
questions.explanation: An intimal tear allows blood to enter the media, creating a false lumen.
questions.pearl: Hypertension is the most common risk factor for aortic dissection.

questions.q: Which classification system is most commonly used for aortic dissections?
questions.explanation: Stanford classifies dissections as Type A (ascending aorta involved) or Type B (ascending aorta not involved).
questions.pearl: Type A dissections usually require emergency surgery.

questions.q: Which symptom is most characteristic of acute aortic dissection?
options: Sudden severe tearing chest or back pain
questions.explanation: Patients classically describe abrupt onset of severe tearing or ripping pain.
questions.pearl: Pain migration may indicate propagation of the dissection.

questions.q: Which imaging study is preferred for a hemodynamically stable patient with suspected aortic dissection?
questions.explanation: CTA rapidly defines the location and extent of dissection and is the preferred initial study in stable patients.
questions.pearl: CTA is also excellent for evaluating aneurysm size.

questions.q: What is the major goal of initial medical management for acute aortic dissection?
options: Lower blood pressure and reduce shear stress
questions.explanation: Anti-impulse therapy with beta-blockers and blood pressure control reduces propagation of the dissection.
questions.pearl: Heart rate control is often achieved before aggressive blood pressure reduction.

questions.q: Which inherited disorder is strongly associated with thoracic aortic aneurysm?
questions.explanation: Marfan syndrome predisposes patients to medial degeneration and thoracic aortic aneurysm.
questions.pearl: Young patients with thoracic aneurysms should be evaluated for genetic syndromes.

questions.q: Which physical examination finding may occur in proximal (Type A) aortic dissection?
questions.explanation: Extension into the aortic root can produce acute aortic regurgitation.
questions.pearl: Pulse deficits increase suspicion for dissection.

questions.q: Which complication is most feared with an enlarging abdominal aortic aneurysm?
questions.explanation: Rupture carries a very high mortality and is the principal indication for elective repair based on aneurysm size.
questions.pearl: Larger aneurysms have a greater annual rupture risk.

questions.q: Which treatment is definitive for most Stanford Type A dissections?
questions.explanation: Type A dissections are surgical emergencies because of the risk of rupture, tamponade, and coronary involvement.
questions.pearl: Mortality rises rapidly if surgical treatment is delayed.

questions.q: What is the most important long-term management strategy after successful treatment of aortic aneurysm or dissection?
options: Lifelong blood pressure control and surveillance imaging
questions.explanation: Strict blood pressure control and periodic imaging are essential to monitor for disease progression or recurrence.
questions.pearl: Lifelong follow-up is required even after successful surgical or endovascular repair.
